label: THE INWARD MIRROR  ·  BOOKLET ONE
title: The Question That Cannot Be Answered
hook: Did you select the exact thought before it appeared?
beats: I began with the ordinary question: what am I here for?
Then another question arose: who is asking?
payoff: Why is the second thought considered more ‘you’ than the first?

label: THE INWARD MIRROR  ·  BOOKLET 2
title: The Guru Who Disappears
hook: The guru does not add a golden box labeled ‘enlightenment.’
beats: He asks who owns the warehouse.
Illumination is not withheld; the instrument keeps insisting on dramatic packaging.
payoff: The knower may still stand outside his knowing, counting it.

label: THE INWARD MIRROR  ·  BOOKLET 3
title: When Silence Began to Dance
hook: There is no second substance outside Reality from which a world could be built.
beats: The unmoving source can appear as every movement without becoming more complete and without losing itself.
payoff: Manifestation does not erase the problem of suffering, but it changes the architecture.

label: THE INWARD MIRROR  ·  BOOKLET 4
title: The Actor Who Forgot He Was Acting
hook: Should not the enlightened person dissolve into excellent background music?
beats: Why does Hanuman still serve, Vyāsa still write, Janaka still rule, and Śiva still meditate?
Liberation while living does not mean the body becomes decorative vapor.
payoff: Freedom is not the absence of conditioning in the instrument; it is the end of absolute identification with it.

label: THE INWARD MIRROR  ·  BOOKLET 5
title: The Freedom to Just Be
hook: Just be does not mean become furniture.
beats: If nothing is lacking in the Self, why act?
The cleaner question is no longer ‘what will happen because of me?’ It is ‘what is required now?’
payoff: Reality has never required irresponsibility as proof of depth.

label: THE INWARD MIRROR  ·  BOOKLET 6
title: The Lover and the Beloved Are One
hook: If everything is One, whom do I worship?
beats: Can the mouth say a name it does not own?
payoff: The wave can bow to the ocean without becoming something other than water.

label: THE INWARD MIRROR  ·  BOOKLET 7
title: Līlā Mādhava
hook: If all is Bhagavān, why this play?
beats: Why does Kṛṣṇa appear to stand on every side of a battlefield?
Why does the pillar have to break?
payoff: It means expression without deficiency, action without the burden of self-completion.
